name: Urinary antibacterials
summary: Antibiotics used for urinary tract infections. The NHS describes nitrofurantoin as a medicine to treat urinary tract infections such as cystitis, and trimethoprim is also an NHS-described antibiotic for urinary tract infections.
mechanism: Nitrofurantoin reaches useful concentrations only in urine, so it is used for lower urinary tract infections such as cystitis and is unsuitable for upper infections of the kidneys.
cautions: The NHS lists a past allergic reaction, a lung condition, severe kidney problems, diabetes, anaemia or vitamin B deficiency, and porphyria among the reasons nitrofurantoin may not be suitable.
The NHS says nitrofurantoin can usually be taken in earlier pregnancy, but a doctor may not recommend it later because it can affect the baby's red blood cells.
For trimethoprim, the NHS lists an allergic reaction, liver or kidney problems and blood disorders such as porphyria among the reasons it may not be suitable.
The NHS says trimethoprim can lower folic acid levels and is not usually recommended in early pregnancy.
classEffects: Nausea, diarrhoea, loss of appetite, headaches and dark yellow or brown urine are common side effects of nitrofurantoin, and usually go away when it is stopped.
Itching or a skin rash may occur with trimethoprim, and these effects are usually mild and short-lived, according to the NHS.
Serious reactions to nitrofurantoin, such as swelling of the throat or tongue or difficulty breathing, are rare; the NHS lists these as symptoms of anaphylaxis, which needs a 999 call.
